parts.text:
Construct several candidate monospaced bitmap-font designs for the Gemini Supervisor reading-room cards. Each glyph cell is exactly 18 pixels wide by 20 pixels high. The visual inspiration should come from High Middle Ages Germanic/Gothic scriptorium hands: Textura/Proto-Gothic/early Gothic book-hand characteristics, angular broken strokes, vertical emphasis, compact forms, and manuscript character, but this is an AI-reading challenge, so OCR/vision readability is the primary requirement. Do not simply name existing fonts; construct usable candidate glyph systems.

Produce 3 distinct candidates, from least decorative/most readable to more strongly Gothic while still reliably distinguishable at 18x20. For each candidate: (1) state the design rules and stroke geometry; (2) define enough representative uppercase, lowercase, digits, and punctuation glyphs as exact 18x20 binary bitmap rows to demonstrate the system; include at minimum A-Z, a-z, 0-9, space, and the punctuation characters commonly required by Markdown/JSON/code: . , : ; ! ? ' " ` - _ + = / \ | ( ) [ ] { } < > # * & % $ @ ^ ~; (3) every glyph must occupy exactly 18 columns x 20 rows; (4) avoid ambiguous pairs such as I/l/1, O/0, rn/m, c/e, {/(, and quote/backtick confusion; (5) keep a consistent baseline, x-height, cap height, and internal margins; (6) give a compact machine-consumable JavaScript representation, preferably glyph => array of twenty 18-bit row strings, so a renderer can draw raw RGB cards without relying on an installed font; (7) include a short preview string recommendation that exercises the ambiguity cases.

The card geometry is fixed at 1440x900, with 80 columns x 45 rows, so each glyph cell must remain exactly 18x20. Do not change the cell geometry. Return concrete font data/code rather than general typography advice.
